case.machine: Battery-electric shuttle (synthetic), 100 Ah pack, BMS and VCU logs
case.reported: The shuttle lost drive power and would not move.
rules: Fault level 1 and 2 permit high voltage; level 3 is the protective shutdown and should stay latched
case.title: Parked shuttle loses high voltage after an undervoltage trip, then is restarted

conditional_leading.condition: the chemistry has a flat OCV plateau (e.g. LFP)
conditional_leading.statement: If the pack's chemistry has a flat OCV plateau (for example LFP), the SOC estimate drifting between calibration anchors is the explanation to check first (reference knowledge, not this record). Confirm the chemistry and read the history since the last full charge.

hypotheses.label: HV lost
hypotheses.statement: High voltage was lost (fault, t=803.02 s): the machine could not drive.

hypotheses.label: Under-voltage protection
missing: The customer's protection specification (thresholds, delays, required order) to judge whether the sequence was correct
hypotheses.statement: The contactors opened as the BMS's protective response to a cell under-voltage escalation.
hypotheses.status_reason: the escalation preceded the opening; that order fits a protective action. Order is not proof of cause; the protection explains HOW HV was lost, not WHY the cells were that low.

hypotheses.label: SOC estimation / calibration error
missing: SOC algorithm: when OCV, full-charge and low-end corrections trigger
Charge and calibration history since the last full charge
The chemistry's OCV curve at temperature, to read SOC from the rested voltage (constant offset, growth with throughput and growth with time point to different causes)
SOC following the measured charge is not independent evidence (SOC is counted from that current): it shows the estimator counted, not that the current or the capacity is right

record_evidence.claim: The SOC already overstated the charge actually available by about 43 pp at the first record, and inside the record it fell only by the charge counted (ratio 0.96, 1.08): the error accumulated BEFORE the record, since the estimator's last calibration anchor. The decisive evidence is the history since that anchor, not another recording of the same signals.
A 29 pp correction moved the SOC with almost no counted charge: the estimate was wrong, the charge was not lost in seconds.

hypotheses.statement: The SOC estimate had drifted high (coulomb counting without effective correction) and was only corrected at the under-voltage alarm.
hypotheses.status_reason: consistent with all recorded evidence; the recorded data does not separate it from B, C

hypotheses.label: Usable capacity far below the stated parameter
missing: An existing, independently metered charge/discharge record (before any controlled capacity test: cycling a possibly faulty pack is itself a risk)
Pack build record: the capacity parameter's origin
The chemistry's OCV curve at temperature, to read SOC from the rested voltage (constant offset, growth with throughput and growth with time point to different causes)
hypotheses.statement: The pack's usable capacity is far below the capacity the SOC is computed against (fade, or a wrong parameter).
hypotheses.status_reason: consistent with all recorded evidence; the recorded data does not separate it from A, C

hypotheses.label: Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor
missing: Independent current measurement against the BMS reading
Standstill load list: which loads bypass the current sensor
The chemistry's OCV curve at temperature, to read SOC from the rested voltage (constant offset, growth with throughput and growth with time point to different causes)
hypotheses.statement: The BMS current sensor under-reads, or some load draws from the pack upstream of it, so counted charge is below real discharge.
hypotheses.status_reason: consistent with all recorded evidence; the recorded data does not separate it from A, B

hypotheses.label: Weak cell / imbalance
missing: Rest voltage of every cell (not only highest/lowest)
Capacity test with all cell voltages logged

Whether the weak cell is degraded or only out of balance: which cell reaches the voltage limits first in an existing, independently metered charge/discharge record (initial balance, temperature and balancing accounted for)
hypotheses.statement: One cell (or a few) is weaker or poorly balanced and reaches the cutoff first.
hypotheses.status_reason: the highest cell was also depleted (pack-wide decline larger than the cell spread), and the SOC accounting discrepancy is pack-level: a weak cell can be an additional contributor, not the whole explanation

hypotheses.label: Cell-voltage sensing or harness fault
missing: Inspection of the cell sense harness and connectors (qualified personnel)
An independent voltage reference on the suspect cells: BMS-reported voltages alone cannot exclude a sensing error
hypotheses.statement: The low cell reading is a sensing error (sense lead, connector, measurement channel).
hypotheses.status_reason: smooth decline, pack-wide fall and physical rest recovery point against a sensing fault; no direct inspection excludes it

hypotheses.label: Contactor, VCU or insulation event first
missing: Insulation readings in a usable range (the recorded field may be saturated)
Contactor command signals (only feedback is recorded)
hypotheses.statement: A contactor, VCU or insulation fault came first and the battery alarms followed.
hypotheses.status_reason: the recorded order runs from cell under-voltage to contactor opening, not the reverse

safety_holds.action: MEAS-CELL-REST by a trained technician; if any cell is below the manufacturer's recovery limit, follow the manufacturer's procedure with HV-qualified staff before any charge or HV closure

provenance.status: encoded by Veyra; not a customer specification and not yet reviewed by the customer

safety_holds.title: Do not close HV or charge again until every cell's rest voltage has been assessed
safety_holds.type: safety precaution, not a finding of fault
safety_holds.why: While HV was on again, the lowest cell reached 2.407 V (closure 1 at 2201.02 s), below the 2.500 V at which the original protective trip fired. Over-discharge risk for the affected cells is an engineering question, not a conclusion of this check.

alignment.statement: Aligned by charge removed in fault, the persistently lowest cell reached 2.95, 2.90, 2.85 V 1.02–1.50 Ah before the highest cell (the offset changes), about 9.4 min at the 8.0 A that flowed meanwhile. Against an SOC discrepancy of about 42.6 Ah, the weakest cell accounts for about 3% of it: it sets WHEN the usable charge ended, not the SIZE of the discrepancy. The offset is observed over about 0.7 Ah of discharge; a capacity difference smaller than that resolution cannot be told from imbalance.

energy_shortfall_overstatement_pp.meaning: how far the first recorded SOC overstated the charge actually delivered to cutoff

quantities.note: These are different quantities: the correction is one abrupt estimator step inside the fault window; the shortfall spans windows and includes an estimate for unrecorded time. Do not add or substitute one for the other.

soc_correction_pp.meaning: abrupt SOC re-statement by the estimator, not explained by measured charge

findings.statement: Customer-confirmed: level 3 blocks HV. Every closure was made with the weakest cell at 2.680–2.680 V, above the 2.500 V at which level 3 fired: the rest recovery lifted the cell back over the blocking threshold before each closure.
2 closure(s) completed with an escalation already reported (level(s) 2). Customer-confirmed rule: these levels permit HV, so this is by design.

The top protective level did not persist across the power cycle: after each reset the system authorised HV again, and 2 of 2 closures ended in another protective shutdown. Customer-confirmed rule: level 3 is meant to latch, so this deviates from the design.

restarts.statement: Customer-confirmed: level 3 blocks HV. Every closure was made with the weakest cell at 2.680–2.680 V, above the 2.500 V at which level 3 fired: the rest recovery lifted the cell back over the blocking threshold before each closure. 2 closure(s) completed with an escalation already reported (level(s) 2). Customer-confirmed rule: these levels permit HV, so this is by design. The top protective level did not persist across the power cycle: after each reset the system authorised HV again, and 2 of 2 closures ended in another protective shutdown. Customer-confirmed rule: level 3 is meant to latch, so this deviates from the design.

findings.statement: The DC/DC reported off at t=802.04 s, yet 8.0 A still flowed until the contactors opened: the continuous load is not only the DC/DC.

values from different messages are joined on the latest sample at or before each instant
sequence.statement: Around the protective shutdown in fault (escalation t=800.0 s, contactors open t=803.02 s): t=800.0 s  bms_fault_level: 2 -> 3; t=800.0 s  bms_state: HV on (0) -> HV not allowed (5); t=800.24 s  power_state: READY (4) -> ACC (3); t=802.04 s  dcdc_state: working (1) -> off (0); t=803.02 s  main_negative_closed: 1 -> 0; t=803.02 s  main_positive_closed: 1 -> 0. Order is consistent with a protective response; order is not proof of cause.

items.statement: With both contactors reported open, 2 of 4,088 current samples are not zero: either a sensor offset or current flowing despite the reported open state.

signals.statement: With both contactors reported open, 2 of 4,088 current samples are not zero: either a sensor offset or current flowing despite the reported open state.

symptom.statement: No drive request and no movement in any recorded frame. The record does not show the reported symptom as stated: no drive request was refused, because none was made. The question becomes why a stationary machine reached a protective state, not why it would not drive.

value.reported: The shuttle lost drive power and would not move.

limits: assumes round thresholds on a 0.05 grid and a fixed delay; hysteresis and filtering are not visible
thresholds.statement: Inferred from the record (the specification decides): level 1 at t=0.0 s with min_cell_voltage 2.95 -> threshold about 2.95 (first crossed 0.68 s earlier); level 2 at t=600.0 s with min_cell_voltage 2.75 -> threshold about 2.75 (first crossed 0.08 s earlier); level 3 at t=800.0 s with min_cell_voltage 2.5001 -> threshold about 2.55 (first crossed 39.98 s earlier).
